C-46, Part XII.2 (offences for laundering proceeds of crime); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 30.2 et seq. (Quebec significant-control declaration for registered partnerships and legal persons); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the general partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the general partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the jurisdiction of execution, with certified French translation prepared by an OTTIAQ-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority and public records office of the UBO's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, the general partner, and the franchise principal against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada, issued under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), the United Nations Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the RCMP and OSFI watchlists, and FINTRAC risk-assessment benchmarks. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any domestic or foreign Politically Exposed Person, close associate, or head of an international organization as defined in SOR/2002-184. Any positive sanctions hit constitutes an automatic name-clearance and registration rejection ground. The franchise is classified Low_Risk_Standard for FINTRAC purposes, but a written AML/CFT risk assessment, $10,000+ cash transaction reporting, and suspicious-transaction reporting (STR) framework under PCMLTFA s. 7.1 must be operational before collection of the first franchise royalty wire or local POS settlement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online name reservation and enterprise registration platform, accessible via https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, ss. 23-26: the registered name of an enterprise in Quebec must be predominantly in French; a non-French corporate name may be registered only with a French trade name or general partner designation of the form 'Boba The L.P.' / 'societe en commandite' (S.E.C.); the French-language name must appear with equal or greater prominence in all franchise agreements, signage, and disclosures; all UBO names in non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters with a certified transliteration, and the associated English-to-French translation must be certified by a member of OTTIAQ.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name-rejection decision, the applicant must obtain the written refusal memorandum from the Registraire des entreprises citing the statutory basis; file a request for administrative review within 30 days under art. 47 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; attach a certified French translation of the disputed suffix and a revised predominantly-French name proposal; if the administrative review is denied, appeal to the Court of Quebec (commercial chamber) within 30 days of the Director's written confirmation; concurrently, file a fresh name reservation application with a distinct French distinct element to avoid franchise-launch delay; an extension of the 90-day reservation period is not available, but re-submission of an identical name is permitted after the statutory waiting period if no conflicting third-party registration arises.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.entity_form_notation: The limited partnership must be designated as 'societe en commandite' or by the approved French abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; the English abbreviation 'L.P.' is accepted as a secondary designation only where the name remains predominantly French.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. The Registraire des entreprises accepts a virtual-office or registered-agent address for the delivery of official notices and service of process; however, the limited partnership must maintain a physical place of business in Quebec for the general partner's local mandate, and a purely postal virtual address is insufficient to satisfy Revenu Quebec, municipal food-establishment licensing, or MAPAQ import requirements for the bubble-tea syrup supply chain. A physical Quebec warehouse or franchise unit must be established before the first MAPAQ food-import permit and municipal restaurant/beverage licence are issued.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: estimated 10-15% probability of an unannounced commercial-substance inspection by the Registraire des entreprises or Revenu Quebec within the first 12 months of registration, increasing to 20-25% where the declared registered office is a virtual office only or where MAPAQ food-import documentation is incomplete; with a real Quebec warehouse or franchise unit and local accounting records in place, the annual inspection probability is reduced below 5%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Book 4, Title 3, arts. 2236-2262 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 14-35 (registration obligation, declaration contents, sanctions); Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1 (filing modalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec Enterprise Registrar, online portal CléQC
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation – Société en commandite (Declaration of Registration – Limited Partnership, Form E-2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; contributions may be in money, property, or services; no escrow account or bank attestation is required by law. Limited partners' liability is capped at their subscribed contribution, which must be recorded in the partnership agreement and capital schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a board meeting of [GP Corp.], the sole general partner of [LP Name] (the "Partnership"), the following resolutions were adopted unanimously: (1) Subscription: the board approved the general partner's capital contribution and the limited partners' initial subscriptions per the Partnership Agreement dated [Date]; (2) Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at [Address], Quebec, and the General Partner is directed to execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (3) Officers: [Name] is appointed Manager and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each authorized to open bank accounts, file regulatory returns, and represent the Partnership before government agencies. All prior acts in furtherance are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Central Enterprise Register (CléQC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name reservation search in the REQ's online register to confirm the proposed distinctive name of the société en commandite is available and not confusingly similar; file Form REN-1 (Demande de réservation de nom) via CléQC. The reservation is valid for 120 days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Form REN-1 (Demande de réservation de nom)
Consent letter from any individual whose personal name appears in the corporate name
Proposed partnership name in French or bilingual format
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, request reconsideration by REQ within 30 days, or submit an amended declaration selecting a new distinctive name pursuant to s. 32 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution and Attestation of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / private counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the corporate general partner is validly incorporated or registered under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec) or the Canada Business Corporations Act; obtain an up-to-date attestation de mise à jour (certificate of status) from REQ; adopt a general partner board resolution consenting to act as general partner of the limited partnership.
required_dossiers: Up-to-date REQ attestation (attestation de mise à jour) for the general partner
General partner board resolution consenting to act
Updated annual declaration of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Complete any missing annual declarations for the general partner and refile a corrected attestation before the declaration filing; late filings may incur penalty under s. 99 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) in French, providing for the partnership name, capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, management powers of the general partner, limited partners' restricted participation, transfer restrictions, and dissolution events. Notarization is optional but recommended for evidentiary weight and third-party reliance.
required_dossiers: Schedule of contributions of each limited partner
Certificate of address for the registered office in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a supplementary agreement or a réctificatif signed by all partners to cure defects; the corrected agreement is binding from the date of signature if in compliance with arts. 2236-2262 CCQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online filing via CléQC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation (Form E-2) to REQ, indicating the legal form (société en commandite), declared name, registered office in Quebec, identification and capacity of each general partner, the express statement that partners' liability is limited, and NAICS 2022 code 722515 for beverage service. Pay the statutory filing fee of approximately CAD 85.60 (approximately USD 63).
required_dossiers: Proof of Quebec registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, file a corrective declaration (déclaration modificative) within 30 days; request administrative review under s. 80 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Account and Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the limited partnership for QST (TVQ) and GST/HST (TPS/TVH) accounts; obtain or update the CRA business number (BN); register as an employer with the CNESST for workplace insurance; the partnership files information return T5013 and the general partner coordinates all compliance filings due to the pass-through tax model.
required_dossiers: Estimated payroll and sales thresholds for QST/GST enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use Revenu Québec's 'Mes services en ligne' portal to amend the registration; contact the business helpline to reconcile discrepancies before the first filing period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal – Service des permis d'affaires), Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business license (permis) for food beverage service; obtain a building permit and fire safety certificate from the RBQ/local fire department for the syrup production and storage areas; register the workplace establishment with CNESST; obtain the MAPAQ food establishment permit before starting production of syrups.
required_dossiers: Floor plans and structural load report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct zoning, fire safety, and structural deficiencies identified in the inspection report; file a modification request with the municipality if the building classification changes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) and Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Établissement alimentaire permit under the Food Products Act (CQLR c P-29) and Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence (SFC-LIC) for manufacturing and distribution of bubble tea syrups and concentrate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration only; the proposed syrup manufacturing and beverage franchising activity is below the threshold for a full EIA report under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23). Submit a registration/declaration of conformity confirming zero significant discharge and adherence to municipal pre-treatment requirements.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with the Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment works (CQLR c Q-2, r. 34.1) – BOD5 ≤ 150 mg/L, TSS ≤ 150 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5, oils and greases ≤ 15 mg/L, or obtain a municipal pre-treatment agreement. Air/VOCs: comply with the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) emission thresholds and odor control provisions for food processing. Waste: comply with the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products (CQLR c Q-2, r. 46.1) for packaging, beverage containers, and organic residue diversion.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local fire safety service and RBQ under the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1); structural load inspection report for kitchen, syrup storage, and warehousing areas; CNESST workplace establishment registration and health-and-safety program; MAPAQ pre-occupational sanitation inspection for food-contact surfaces; municipal zoning, sanitation, and water connection clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal GST/HST and income tax: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC), portal canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; Quebec QST and collection of federal GST/HST in Quebec under a collection agreement: Revenu Québec, portal revenuquebec.ca; enterprise registration: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), portal registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership (CA_LP) must first register the partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and disclose the general and limited partners; it then opens a single Revenu Québec registrant file for GST/HST plus QST through Revenu Québec's online portal, or with CRA's Business Registration Online using the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN). A non-resident LP without a physical establishment in Quebec must appoint a service representative/mandatary in Quebec and file the partnership identity declaration with CRA and Revenu Québec. Revenu Québec issues the 16-character QST registration identifier (e.g., 1234567890 TQ 0001); the LP must file the T5013 Partnership Information Return and the Quebec equivalent (CO-17) annually.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box election. A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) is fiscally transparent for Canadian federal and Quebec income tax: partners, not the LP, bear tax on partnership income. Available domestic elections include: (i) non-calendar-year partnership fiscal period election under ITA s. 249.1(8), mirrored in Quebec; (ii) ITA s. 216 election permitting a non-resident partner to compute Part I tax on active business income instead of Part XIII withholding; (iii) hybrid mismatch and dual consolidated loss limitations under ITA s. 18.4; and (iv) for U.S. federal purposes, a Form 8832 check-the-box election to treat the LP as an association taxable as a corporation, the resulting entity classification being recognized for Canada-U.S. treaty purposes in accordance with CRA administrative entity-classification guidance, while preserving fiscally transparent treatment where the LP is not an electing eligible entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST/HST (Excise Tax Act, Part IX) and Quebec QST (Loi sur la taxe de vente du Québec) — value-added tax regime administered jointly in Quebec by Revenu Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (annual worldwide taxable supplies for the small-supplier exception); no registration threshold for non-resident suppliers of digital services or intangible property to Canadian/Quebec consumers effective GST/HST July 1, 2021 and QST January 1, 2019; franchise royalty and syrup B2B supplies to non-residents require standard registration once the CAD 30,000 turnover threshold is exceeded
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory B2B real-time clearance, API fiscal reporting, or digital stamping regime is in force in Canada or Quebec; GST/HST returns are filed electronically through CRA NETFILE (GST34) and QST returns through Revenu Québec; customs and export reporting is digital via Canada Border Services Agency using the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED), CERS, and the Single Window Initiative; Revenu Québec mandates electronic filing of RL/T4/CO-17 information slips and requires large businesses to transmit certain data via EDI/XML; all books, records, invoices, and e-invoicing documents must be retained for six years from the end of the relevant period, or longer with CRA consent, for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada where the supplier exports or causes the export under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 1 and 14, with mirrored QST provisions under the LTVQ; syrup inventory shipped to foreign franchisees qualifies where the goods leave Canada and the franchisee obtains possession and use outside Canada. Services and royalties supplied to non-resident franchisees are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 7 and 23 when the recipient is a non-resident not present in Canada at the time the service is performed, the franchise licence is not exploited in Canada, and no Canadian goods or services are transferred in connection with the supply; Revenu Québec applies the same zero-rating tests for QST purposes. The master franchise and trademark licence contracts must be structured and invoiced to offshore franchise entities so that Canadian nexus (Canadian employees, Canadian customers, Canadian locations) is not incidentally created, which would disqualify zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A or electronic export declaration via CERS/CAED)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (through-export evidence with forwarder cargo control documents)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or other bank wire receipt evidencing foreign-currency settlement
Commercial invoice showing EXW/FOB terms, destination, and consignee outside Canada
Packing slips, warehouse gate receipts, and container tracking records demonstrating physical removal from Canada
Signed master franchise and licence agreements with each non-resident franchisee, together with their local VAT/GST registration certificates
Customs broker instruction sheets and carrier manifests matched to the LP's T5013 allocation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years for ordinary adjustments, extended to seven years where misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is shown (ETA s. 298); Revenu Québec applies the same general windows and a six-year window for unreported earnings. Where zero-rating is not substantiated, CRA and Revenu Québec impose retroactive GST/HST plus QST of 14.975% on the assessed taxable receipts, with prescribed daily compound interest and civil penalties under ETA s. 280 (false entries) and s. 285.1 (25% of any overclaimed refund or rebate); gross negligence and wilful evasion attract penalties of up to 50% of tax understated (ITA s. 163(2) and QST Act s. 526), criminal fines up to double the tax evaded, and imprisonment under ETA s. 327 (maximum five years). CRA and Revenu Québec may also recompute franchise, syrup, and royalty transfer prices under ITA s. 247, triggering a 10% adjustment penalty, and may deny input tax credits or refunds until the complete documentary export bundle is produced. Evidentiary sufficiency includes receipt and banking of export proceeds within the 180-day window; failure to satisfy this evidentiary protocol can cause the export zero-rating to be clawed back retroactively with full interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC), with prudential regulation of banks and clearing settlement systems overseen by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign exchange administration and policy enforcement under the Financial Administration Act, the Currency Act, and the Export and Import Permits Act, administered through the Department of Finance Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a freely convertible currency with no exchange control regime for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittances, dividends, royalty payments, and capital outflows are permitted without prior central bank approval, subject to anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds, tax withholding compliance, and financial information reporting. For a Quebec limited partnership, the repatriation of distributable profits to non-resident partners is unrestricted but may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty; no hard convertibility or remittance approval hurdle exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or mandatory currency conversion ratio applies to Canadian export receipts. Exporters may earn, hold, and disburse foreign currency freely. For statistical purposes, transactions exceeding C$10,000 or certain thresholds may require reporting to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and/or Statistics Canada under the Banking Act and the International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS); repatriated funds are not subject to any conversion timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium for directly licensed EMIs; no EU-style EMI passport exists in Canada. Foreign fintechs acting as money transmitters or payment service providers must register as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA and, for activity in Quebec, may require additional licensing from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). A fully regulated Canadian chartered bank remains the highest-viability treasury backbone; offshore digital EMIs can be used as ancillary collection or disbursement tools only where the underlying funds flow is transparent and all Canadian reporting obligations are satisfied.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted for Canadian low-risk corporate clients if reliable identification is performed through digital identity verification, but banks retain discretion to require an in-person or video interview. For a Quebec limited partnership with a non-resident general partner or foreign authorized signatories, at least one senior principal (partner or director) may be required to complete a verification interview and provide notarized or apostilled corporate and KYC documents. The account mandate must evidence on-chain delegated authority from the LP and all beneficial owners above the 25% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented beneficial ownership requiring consolidation across transnational franchise and syrup supply chain entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart with ultimate beneficial owners, certified copies of registry extracts from Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), LP agreement, trust declarations if applicable, and sworn statutory declarations confirming source of funds and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident general partner or foreign investor without verifiable Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport, tax residency certificates, apostilled incorporation certificates, powers of attorney, board resolutions authorizing the Quebec LP relationship, and a written compliance memorandum explaining the standardized ISIC 5610 boba tea franchise business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume royalty and syrup import/export flows inconsistent with initial stated revenue projections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward franchise royalty schedules, master franchise agreements, validated supplier invoices for tea, syrup and packaging, treasury forecast model, and audited or internally prepared projected financial statements for 24 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned jurisdictions or politically exposed persons in the payment chain for international syrup procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP and sanctions screening declarations, underlying bills of lading, incoterms contracts, freight forwarder engagement letters, and an executed internal sanctions compliance policy restricting prohibited counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Quebec LP receiving equity capital from its non-resident parent or franchise investors, funds should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with payment field 70 referencing 'Capital contribution to CA_LP / equity injection' and purpose code consistent with direct investment (ISO 20022 camt purpose 'INVEST' or 'MULTI' where applicable). No exchange control filing is required, but the receiving Canadian bank will require a completed corporate resolution, confirmation of no disgorgement under the Competition Act, and supporting wire instructions matching the bank account mandate. The amount must be recorded for tax and capital account reporting in accordance with the Income Tax Act and Quebec taxation rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for syrup and equipment procurement are executed by SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-bank payments, with documentary collection or irrevocable commercial letters of credit (L/C) used for high-value, recurring cross-border shipments. Payments must identify the underlying commercial invoice, HS tariff classification, and SWIFT business identifier code (BIC) of the beneficiary. For royalty withdrawals and distributions to non-resident partners, use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 where appropriate, and remit through a Canadian bank with encoded withholding-tax instructions to satisfy Part XIII withholding obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forwards (deliverable forwards on USD/CAD, CNY/CAD, and other G10 and Asian currency pairs) executed under standard ISDA and Canadian FX master agreements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies subject to limited onshore forward markets where the underlying export/syrup trade creates a genuine economic exposure and the instrument is documented as a derivative under OSFI guidelines
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD/CAD liability and receivable mismatches, fully documented with collateral arrangements and hedge accounting designation
FX options and option collars purchased or structured for capital-protection hedging of foreign-currency franchise royalties

Interest rate and cross-currency basis swaps used only to align the treasury portfolio with underlying operational cash flows, provided all derivative transactions are within the corporate mandate approved by the LP's partners and compliant with Canadian derivative trade reporting rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, confirming legal form, registered office, general and limited partners, and activity codes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually no later than 15 days after the last day of the month in which the registration anniversary falls (e.g., a June registration anniversary triggers a July 15 deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional late-filing governmental fee applies; the Registrar publicly notes the default, suspension of the benefit of legal publicity (opposability) against third parties follows, and after two consecutive years of non-filing the Quebec Enterprise Registrar may administratively strike the limited partnership off the register after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Income Information Return, including Schedule 50 and partner allocation slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Partnerships and Trusts Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a partnership with a corporate general partner or any non-resident partner, with a calendar-year fiscal period, due November 30 of the following calendar year; for all-individual partnerships, due March 31 immediately following the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day for each day the T5013 return is late, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; continued non-compliance can trigger partner-level reassessments and an administrative information-return demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information slip (TP-31) and provincial partner allocation reporting for Quebec-source royalty and franchise income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed on the same timeline as the federal T5013 return for the same fiscal period; Quebec partners report allocated income on their TP-1 returns by May 1 for individuals and June 15 for self-employed filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec may impose a 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month compounded on unpaid partner balances to a maximum of 12%; enterprise registration suspension is also triggered through the Enterprise Registrar for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed solely by the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises on a limited partnership; a mandatory audit is triggered when (i) the LP or its general partner is a reporting issuer under the Quebec Securities Act, (ii) franchise, bank, or partnership agreements require certified financial statements, (iii) the consolidated group meets public-accountability thresholds under IFRS, or (iv) CRA or Revenu Québec exercises statutory audit and records-inspection powers
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private limited partnerships in Quebec prepare financial statements under Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II); IFRS (Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable entities and is adopted where the global boba tea franchise consolidates Quebec royalty flows into cross-border group accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec limited partnerships must file an annual declaration restating, as at the anniversary date, the name and domicile of every general partner (commandité) and limited partner (commanditaire); legal-person partners require look-through disclosure of directors or trustees; any transfer, allotment, or redemption of partnership interests during the year must be declared to the Enterprise Registrar within 15 days of the transaction, and the annual confirmation recertifies the resulting beneficial-ownership roster and the 25%-or-more ownership disclosure threshold
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220–480 per year (CAD 300–650) for a professional registered office and service agent in Montreal or Quebec City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–15,000 (CAD 8,000–20,000) for a full-scope certified audit of a mid-size franchise royalty limited partnership under ASPE or IFRS, subject to unit count and consolidated reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Not applicable at entity level; limited partnership is fiscally transparent. Corporate partners face a combined Canadian federal + Quebec headline rate of 26.5% (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec) on allocated income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For Canadian-controlled private corporation partners: Small Business Deduction reduces combined rate to approximately 13.2% (9% federal + 4% Quebec) on first CAD 500,000 of active business income. Federal SR&ED investment tax credits (15% to 35%) and Quebec innovation credits may further reduce effective tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return (CRA My Business Account / Netfile). Quebec: TP-600 – Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes (Revenu Québec TSO / CLICK software).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013: within 5 months after fiscal year-end (6 months if any partner is a non-resident). TP-600: within 6 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and registered office address of the limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide exact registered name in Latin script; address must be the registered office in Quebec, not a forwarding address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period beginning and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar year is standard; if a different period is used, ensure all partner allocations are reported consistently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code (NAICS 722515) and description.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the code for franchise tea/beverage operations; note whether income is from franchising royalties or direct retail sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, tax number, and share of each partner in income (loss).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, provide complete name, country of residence, and Canadian non-resident tax identification number; attach NR301/NR301A forms if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income (loss) allocated to each partner per the LP agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations must follow the economic substance of the LP agreement; non-resident partners are taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: CRA charges CAD 25 per partner per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); Revenu Québec charges CAD 50 per day (maximum CAD 5,000). Intentional omissions trigger an additional penalty equal to 5% of the unreported amount plus 1% per month up to 12%, and criminal prosecution under s.239 ITA.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII); not applicable at LP level – the partnership is fiscally transparent and does not pay dividends. Non-resident partners are taxed on their share of Canadian-source income and may face Part XIII withholding on distributions of passive income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partners claiming DTA relief must submit a completed Form NR301 (Quebec) and/or NR301A (federal) to the withholding agent before payment. Supporting documents: current Certificate of Residence (e.g., US Form 6166), statement of treaty entitlement, and LP agreement evidencing profit-sharing. Revenu Québec and CRA may require advance clearance under Tax Administration Act for certain hybrid structures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: federal statutory WHT 25%, reduced to 0% under Canada–US DTA (unless by non-resident related party with excessive debt levels). Royalties for trademark/franchise IP: statutory 25%, Canada–US DTA generally 15% (10% for patents, designs, or industrial process royalties). No Quebec provincial withholding on royalties or interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File required for fiscal periods if the partnership or its franchise group has gross revenue exceeding CAD 15 million or non-arm's length cross-border transaction value exceeding CAD 5 million. Below thresholds, a simplified TP policy memorandum and contemporaneous benchmarking report are strongly recommended to support arm's length pricing.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for LPs. However, the federal GAAR (Income Tax Act s.245) and Quebec GAAR (Tax Administration Act ss.1079.14-1079.18) deny tax benefits from transactions without genuine economic substance. For an LP franchisor, CRA/Revenu Québec may recharacterize intercompany royalty streams or expense allocations if the partnership lacks real operational authority, physical presence, or actual decision-making over franchise operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to report franchise royalty revenue or claiming fictitious franchise network expenses; shifting income to offshore shell entities without commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal: prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239(1) – fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Quebec: Tax Administration Act penalties and criminal sanctions for false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and controlling directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties; civil restitution orders may freeze personal assets; travel bans can be imposed under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registration of a limited partnership with no physical location in Quebec, no employees, and no genuine business activity while claiming entitlement to treaty benefits or allocating income to non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revenu Québec may annul LP registration and reassess income at the highest marginal rate; application of Canada’s GAAR to disregard transactions; administrative penalties up to CAD 10,000 per false statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil under Civil Code of Québec art. 317; partners become personally liable for the partnership’s tax debts; directors face disqualification and up to 3 years imprisonment for fraudulent corporate activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash franchise fees above CAD 10,000 without FINTRAC reporting; structuring cash deposits to avoid reporting; transferring funds to high-risk jurisdictions without adequate KYC verification of franchisees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2 million per violation for businesses; criminal money-laundering offense under Criminal Code s.462.31 – imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers personally liable for failure to report; assets subject to civil forfeiture; travel bans and arrest warrants can be issued; partnership property may be seized pending investigation.
